record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.context_brief: tensor products of Banach lattice algebras
record.original_question: Develop a categorically satisfying theory of Banach lattice algebra tensor products. Presumably the Fremlin tensor product of Banach lattices would be a starting point, but this is not entirely clear.

evidence.quote: Develop a categorically satisfying theory of Banach lattice algebra tensor products. Presumably the Fremlin tensor product of Banach lattices would be a starting point, but this is not entirely clear.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach lattice is a real Banach space E equipped with a partial order ≤ making it a vector lattice (Riesz space) such that |x| ≤ |y| implies ‖x‖ ≤ ‖y‖, where |x| = x ∨ (−x). A Banach lattice algebra is a Banach lattice A that is simultaneously a Banach algebra and whose product is positive in the sense that a, b ≥ 0 implies ab ≥ 0. The Fremlin projective tensor product E ⊗̂_F F of two Banach lattices E and F is the completion, with respect to the Fremlin positive projective norm, of the Riesz space tensor product of E and F; it is characterized by a universal property for positive bilinear maps that are jointly continuous and lattice-bilinear.

Task: Construct a theory of tensor products in the category of Banach lattice algebras (with morphisms being contractive lattice-algebra homomorphisms, or another natural choice of morphism) that is categorically satisfactory. Specifically:

(a) Define a tensor product A ⊗ B of Banach lattice algebras A and B which is itself a Banach lattice algebra, in a way that is functorial in both arguments.
(b) Establish a universal property characterizing this construction up to isometric Banach-lattice-algebra isomorphism.
(c) Determine to what extent the Fremlin projective tensor product of the underlying Banach lattices can serve as the starting point for such a construction, and identify the additional structure or modifications (e.g., for f-algebras, almost f-algebras, or d-algebras) needed to obtain a well-behaved tensor product.
(d) Verify natural categorical properties such as associativity, commutativity, behavior of identities, and compatibility with relevant subcategories (e.g., commutative algebras, f-algebras).
artifact.category_tag: Banach lattice algebras and tensor products
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has constructed a Banach lattice algebra structure on the Fremlin projective tensor product of two Banach lattice algebras, with the canonical product (a⊗b)(x⊗y)=ax⊗by extending continuously, and has shown that the Fremlin projective tensor product of two Banach f-algebras is again a Banach f-algebra, satisfying an appropriate universal property. This provides substantial progress toward a categorical theory, though a fully comprehensive categorical framework covering all variants and morphism classes does not appear to be definitively settled.

status_evidence.title: The Fremlin projective tensor product of Banach lattice algebras
status_evidence.snippet: The canonical product (a⊗b)(x⊗y)=ax⊗by extends to a Banach lattice algebra product on the Fremlin projective tensor product, and the Fremlin projective tensor product of Banach f-algebras is a Banach f-algebra.
status_evidence.claim: A Banach lattice algebra structure on the Fremlin projective tensor product has been constructed, addressing significant portions of the problem.

status_evidence.title: A topology on the Fremlin tensor product between locally solid vector lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Topologies on Fremlin tensor products between locally solid vector lattices with applications.
status_evidence.claim: Further extensions to locally solid vector lattices have been developed.
